committee_name.text: Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee

quote.quote: The Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee met on November 14, 2013 to consider the efficacy and safety of tasimelteon. The majority of the Committee voted in the affirmative to the following questions:

As noted in Dr. Jillapalli's review, The Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee met on November 14, 2013 to consider the efficacy and safety of tasimelteon. The majority of the Committee voted in the affirmative to the following questions:

recommendation.text: Supportive. The majority of the committee voted in the affirmative that Non-24 is appropriate as an indication for an FDA-approved drug therapy, that the clinical endpoints used in the development program were appropriate, that substantial evidence of efficacy had been presented, and that the safety of tasimelteon had been adequately addressed. The review team unanimously recommended approval.

quote.quote: As noted in Dr. Jillapalli's review, The Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee met on November 14, 2013 to consider the efficacy and safety of tasimelteon. The majority of the Committee voted affirmatively on the following questions:

summary: The Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee met on November 14, 2013 and the majority voted affirmatively on all four questions: that Non-24 is an appropriate indication, that the clinical endpoints used were appropriate, that substantial evidence of efficacy had been presented, and that safety had been adequately addressed. The committee's input was supportive and endorsed the division's approach; the review documents describe no AdComm concern that produced a specific change to the approval (no boxed warning, REMS, PMR/PMC, dose, indication, or population restriction tied to the committee). HETLIOZ was approved for Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Disorder consistent with that favorable committee outcome.
